title: Grade 4 Science — Wed, May 27
description: Rocks & Minerals — Day 3 of 5: Minerals and their uses
subject: science

questions.question: What is a mineral?
options: A naturally occurring, solid, non-living substance with a definite chemical composition
questions.explanation: Minerals: naturally occurring, inorganic (not from living things), solid, definite chemical formula, crystal structure. Rocks are made of minerals.

questions.question: How is a mineral different from a rock?
options: Minerals are single pure substances; rocks are mixtures of minerals
Rocks are always harder than minerals
Minerals are found underground; rocks are found above ground
questions.explanation: Granite (rock) is made of quartz + feldspar + mica (minerals). Minerals are the 'ingredients'; rocks are the 'mixture'.

questions.question: Which mineral is the hardest natural substance?
questions.explanation: Diamond = hardness 10 on Mohs scale — the hardest natural mineral. Used for cutting tools, jewellery.

questions.question: Salt (sodium chloride) is a mineral. Where is it found?
options: In seawater, salt lakes, and underground rock salt deposits
questions.explanation: Salt is a naturally occurring mineral found in seawater, salt lakes (like Sambhar Lake, India), and underground halite deposits.

questions.question: Which mineral is used to make pencil 'lead'?
questions.explanation: Pencils use graphite (not lead). Graphite and diamond are both forms of carbon — but graphite is soft and leaves marks.

questions.question: Iron ore (like hematite) is a mineral used to make:
options: Steel and iron products (bridges, buildings, vehicles)
questions.explanation: Iron ore is smelted to extract iron, which is mixed with carbon to make steel — used in construction and manufacturing.

questions.question: Quartz is a very common mineral. It is used to make:
questions.explanation: Quartz (silicon dioxide) is used to make glass. Pure quartz is also used in electronics (computer chips, watches).

questions.question: Which mineral is used in toothpaste to help clean teeth?
questions.explanation: Calcite (calcium carbonate) is a mild abrasive used in toothpaste. It gently scrubs without damaging enamel.

questions.question: Gold and silver are minerals used mainly for:
questions.explanation: Gold and silver: precious metals used in jewellery. Both are excellent electrical conductors used in electronics and wiring.

questions.question: Talc is the softest mineral (hardness 1). What is it used for?
questions.explanation: Talc is so soft it can be powdered easily. Used in talcum powder, baby powder, cosmetics, and as a lubricant.

questions.question: India has rich deposits of which mineral used in jewellery?
questions.explanation: India was historically famous for diamonds (Golconda, now Hyderabad area; Panna in Madhya Pradesh). Also has large mica and iron ore deposits.

questions.question: Mica mineral is known for:
options: Splitting into thin transparent sheets; used in electrical insulation
questions.explanation: Mica splits into thin, flat, transparent sheets. Used in electrical insulation, capacitors, cosmetics (shimmer), and as a window substitute historically.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a mineral?
questions.explanation: Wood comes from living trees — it is organic. Minerals must be inorganic (not from living things). Quartz, diamond, and gold are all minerals.

questions.question: Coal is sometimes called a mineral. Why is it technically NOT a mineral?
options: It was formed from living organisms (plants) — not inorganic
questions.explanation: True minerals must be inorganic. Coal formed from compressed plant matter (organic). So it is classified as a rock, not a mineral.

questions.question: Summary: Why do we need minerals?
options: Minerals are raw materials for glass, metal, electronics, cosmetics, construction, and even health
Minerals are only found in labs
questions.explanation: Minerals are essential raw materials: iron→steel, quartz→glass, graphite→pencils, calcite→toothpaste, gold→electronics, mica→insulation.
